speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and when did you first notice it?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash cause any itching or discomfort for the baby, and have you noticed any similar scaling on his face, neck, or diaper area? I would also like to examine the scalp more closely to assess the thickness of the scales.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal biopsy and the presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead, this presentation is classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis, also known as cradle cap. The family history of psoriasis is a risk factor, but the clinical features and negative biopsy strongly favor seborrheic dermatitis over psoriasis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
